content.user_title: Configure ShellCheck for Reliable Shell Scripts
content.value_statement: Shell scripts often fail because of quoting, portability, and pipeline errors. This skill provides practical ShellCheck configuration, fixes, and workflow integration.
actual_capabilities: Explains ShellCheck installation and version verification across common environments.
Builds project configuration for target shells, enabled checks, exclusions, and external sources.
Explains common diagnostic families and suggests focused corrections.
Provides pre-commit, GitHub Actions, and GitLab CI integration patterns.
Shows scoped warning suppression with documentation for each exclusion.
Covers multi-file checks, parallel linting, caching, and output formats.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples but does not bundle or install ShellCheck.
Examples require adaptation for each repository, shell dialect, and operating system.
Static analysis cannot replace runtime tests for environment-dependent behavior.
The referenced implementation playbook is not included in the audited file structure.

use_cases.title: Add CI linting
use_cases.description: Create a repeatable ShellCheck quality gate for repository shell scripts.

use_cases.title: Resolve diagnostics
use_cases.description: Interpret warning codes and apply fixes without broad rule suppression.

use_cases.title: Improve portability
use_cases.description: Align scripts and configuration with Bash or strict POSIX requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a ShellCheck configuration for a [shell] project. Explain each enabled or disabled rule and provide verification steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Starting ShellCheck in a small repository

prompt_templates.title: Fix reported warnings
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these ShellCheck diagnostics: [diagnostics]. Suggest minimal fixes for [script context] while preserving behavior and portability.
prompt_templates.scenario: Resolving findings in an existing script

prompt_templates.title: Integrate a CI quality gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Design ShellCheck checks for [CI platform]. Cover file discovery, failure behavior, exclusions, output format, and local reproduction.
prompt_templates.scenario: Adding lint enforcement to continuous integration

prompt_templates.title: Audit an advanced linting strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit our ShellCheck configuration and workflow: [details]. Identify portability gaps, unsafe suppressions, performance issues, and a staged remediation plan.
prompt_templates.scenario: Improving lint governance across a large repository

output_examples.input: Configure ShellCheck for a Bash repository with generated vendor scripts.
output_examples.output: Recommended configuration targets Bash, enables optional checks, excludes generated paths in file discovery, and documents every warning suppression.

output_examples.input: Explain a word-splitting warning for an array expansion.
output_examples.output: The review identifies unquoted expansion, recommends quoted array syntax, explains the behavior change, and requests a representative test case.

output_examples.input: Add ShellCheck to a pull request workflow.
output_examples.output: The plan installs a pinned tool version, scans tracked shell files, emits compiler-friendly diagnostics, and fails the job on actionable findings.

best_practices: Match the configured shell dialect to each script interpreter.
Document every exclusion and keep its scope as narrow as possible.
Run the same ShellCheck command locally and in continuous integration.
anti_patterns: Do not disable broad warning groups only to make the pipeline pass.
Do not treat static analysis as a replacement for runtime tests.
Do not scan generated or third-party scripts without an explicit policy.

faq.question: Does this skill install ShellCheck?
faq.answer: No. It provides installation commands and configuration guidance for users to apply in their environment.

faq.question: Which shells does the guidance cover?
faq.answer: It covers Bash, POSIX sh, dash, ksh, and related ShellCheck target settings.

faq.question: Can it explain ShellCheck warning codes?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains common diagnostic groups and shows focused correction patterns.

faq.question: Does it support CI integration?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes patterns for GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, and pre-commit checks.

faq.question: Can it justify warning exclusions?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends narrow exclusions with comments that record the reason.

faq.question: Will ShellCheck prove a script is correct?
faq.answer: No. Runtime tests remain necessary for permissions, external tools, data, and environment-specific behavior.
